summary: Power law y = a · xᵇ. The exponent b controls the curvature; positive b grows superlinearly, negative b decays in a heavy-tailed way.

ranges.phrase: Steep heavy-tailed decay — extreme values are exponentially less likely but still drive most of the variance.
Heavy-tailed but moderate — the largest 1% of observations carry significant weight.
Flat dependence — closer to a constant relationship than a true power law.
Near-linear regime — y scales roughly proportional to x.
Superlinear growth — y rises sharply with x; check for saturation outside the fitted range.
